concerns.text: The Piecewise Linear Regression (PLR) is fit on only four library‑size points (10, 30, 50, 100). With such a sparse grid, estimating a breakpoint (x₀) is under‑determined and may produce unstable or arbitrary results, making the ‘tipping point’ claim empirically weak.

The VIF diagnostic checks collinearity between ‘Library Size’ and ‘Total Redundancy’ (mean pairwise cosine). Because total redundancy inherently scales with the number of skills in the library, these two predictors are not independent; treating them as separate covariates violates the assumption of predictor independence required for valid VIF interpretation.
